policies.summary: For a certified power plant (solar of 75 MW or more, or a smaller one whose applicant opts in), the state preempts regulation and certification of the site, and any conflicting local ordinance or rule is superseded.

A photovoltaic solar facility must be a permitted use in every agricultural land use category and agricultural zoning district in unincorporated areas, subject only to the setbacks and landscaped buffers that apply to similar agricultural uses; county buffer and landscaping rules for solar may not exceed those for comparable permitted uses. Since 2026 solar builders must also follow added stormwater and erosion control practices.

policies.state_body: Florida Siting Board (with the Department of Environmental Protection Siting Coordination Office)
policies.summary: A steam or solar electrical power plant of 75 MW or more must be certified by the state under the Power Plant Siting Act, and a smaller one may opt in; certification replaces local permits. Below 75 MW, solar is decided by local governments, which must treat it as a permitted use in agricultural zoning. No statute gives the state a siting role for wind, which is banned near the coast and offshore.

Florida bans building or expanding any offshore wind energy facility, any wind turbine or wind facility within 1 mile of the coastline or of the Atlantic or Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, and any wind turbine on state waters or submerged lands; turbines installed before July 1, 2024 may keep operating. Turbines covered are those able to produce more than 10 kW.
